sampling_model.design: A two-arm randomized vaccine trial is combined with an external exposure-surveillance sample from the same period-specific target environment.
sampling_model.units: Trial participants are independent draws. Conditional on each realized arm size, the mutually exclusive categories consisting of no first infection and first infection by period and variant are multinomial. Each period-specific external exposure count is multinomial on \(\mathcal V_0\); arbitrary dependence between the two period margins for the same surveillance units is allowed because simultaneous coverage uses a union bound.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\in\{0,1\}\) has known probabilities \(\pi\), and the trial records the period and variant of each first infection.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-arm positivity is standard. Noninfecting-exposure priming is indexed by the disclosed sensitivity value \(\delta\), with \(\delta=0\) giving no priming and \(\delta=1\) permitting unrestricted priming. Fiber-wide period-two vaccine reference-risk positivity is a separate novel, LP-checkable restriction used only for finite Charnes--Cooper endpoints; the extended identified set and exact projection allow zero denominators.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. Zero observed and zero candidate cells are permitted. The sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) is fixed outside these samples; routine negative tests or serial serology do not identify a small \(\delta\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives sharp two-period bounds for a single-pathogen challenge effect from conventional vaccine-trial risks.
Section 4 shows that multi-variant vaccine-effectiveness measures can be time-varying under leaky and all-or-none mechanisms.
The weighted estimating-equation model permits time-varying vaccine efficacy and time-varying pathogen distributions under a marked exposure process.
Case-only strain odds ratios receive a biological relative-efficacy interpretation under stated exposure and susceptibility conditions.
Theorems 1 through 3 identify conditional relative strain efficacy from case-only data under explicit missingness and causal assumptions.
Finite latent response types and linear programming yield tight treatment-effect bounds and attaining distributions.
The paper constructs random regions with uniform asymptotic coverage of an entire identified set or its known image.
Calibrated bootstrap projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions of moment-constrained partially identified parameters.
Derivative-aware resampling is valid for directionally differentiable maps in settings where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
The paper develops a powerful single-pathogen test of treatment-effect constancy and additional waning bounds.

Section 5 defines the marginal time-to-event challenge subtype effect, and the marginal-identification proposition identifies it as a ratio of two observed cause-specific hazard ratios under the paper's stated time-to-event identification and proportionality assumptions.

body.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type now permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and a disclosed \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction; \(\delta=0\) gives no priming and \(\delta=1\) is unrestricted. Pointwise in \(\delta\), one finite common-history polytope exactly represents every law compatible with randomized-trial risks and external exposure margins, its extended reference-mixture ratio set remains sharp at zero denominators, finite reciprocal endpoints follow under the separate LP-audited denominator condition, and a common-law dual certifies strict ratio signs. Results are reported pointwise and over a scientifically justified range \(\mathcal D\), defaulting to \([0,1]\) without a randomized or controlled validation substudy. Open questions cover the Perényi--Stensrud collapse boundary, case-frequency substitution, fixed-fiber policy-mixture sign robustness, and exact multinomial whole-set projection.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under exposure and proportionality restrictions. Neither gives a sharp common-history ratio set from trial first-infection risks plus external variant-exposure margins when a prior exposure that did not infect may alter later controlled susceptibility, nor an observable sign certificate valid pointwise over a disclosed bound on that priming.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target response from the response after a noninfecting exposure; the linear sensitivity value \(\delta\) then restricts their disagreement without replacing external exposure margins by selected case-strain frequencies. Routine negative tests and serial serology do not justify a small \(\delta\), so analysis without a controlled validation substudy spans \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain supplies, pointwise in \(\delta\), exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual with compatible counterlaws. A sensitivity-range envelope reports the set and sign conclusion over \(\mathcal D\). Positivity duality, endpoint sign algebra, biological translation, and the \(K=2\) no-priming lift remain audit or calibration results; the collapse, substitution, radius, and exact-inference frontiers remain open.

body.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws; their multiple-version analysis does not retain external period-specific variant margins or index later controlled response by a prior noninfecting exposure. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) define a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from point-mass controlled-exposure risks and identify it by observed cause-specific hazards under time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality. Their causal coordinates are represented here using \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), with the period-two coordinate explicitly based on \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\); the present external-margin sensitivity fiber is informed by that estimand but does not claim a theorem-level class-inclusion boundary, which remains \(\text{oeq:perenyi-collapse-boundary}\). Tomer and Biccler (2022) show that competing variants can generate temporal movement under specified mechanisms, but do not give a common-history sign certificate under bounded noninfecting-exposure priming or a fixed-fiber mixture radius. Follmann and Huang (2018) use a marked exposure-process model. Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) explain why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external exposure margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the open inference question instead fixes exact multinomial inversion allowing zero cells and projects each \(\delta\)-fiber and its prespecified sensitivity envelope.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) controls whether a single period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest sensitivity range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\). The finite map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.
body.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation are substantive claims pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\). The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), while observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded, not suppressed. The report gives pointwise results and the sharp envelope over a scientifically justified \(\mathcal D\), using \([0,1]\) without controlled validation. Fiber infeasibility is failure and never vacuous positivity. Positivity duality, endpoint sign trichotomy, positive-placebo biological translation, the \(K=2\) lift, and the \(K=1,\delta=0\) reduction are implementation or calibration results. The Perényi--Stensrud collapse boundary, case-frequency invariance, fixed-fiber mixture radius, and exact multinomial projection remain open. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.
